title: Compare tested display formats
citation: Bannister et al. (2021), Improving the visual communication of environmental model projections, Scientific Reports 11, 19157.
illustrates: Ten alternative displays of the same projections; useful for comparing dots, intervals, fans and heatmaps.
regional_adaptation: Start with points and intervals for small ensembles. Test readers' ability to identify magnitude and spread.

title: Explain the interval before presenting results
citation: Müller and Döll (2024), Quantifying and communicating uncertain climate change hazards in participatory climate change adaptation processes, Geoscience Communication 7, 121–144.
rights: CC BY 4.0; retain third-party credits shown in the article, including the source diagram and logos in Figure 3.
illustrates: A teaching graphic for the meaning of percentile boxes in a participatory adaptation process.
regional_adaptation: Label percentiles as summaries of the selected ensemble. They are not automatically probabilities of future outcomes.

title: Show how the evidence was produced
citation: Müller and Döll (2024), Quantifying and communicating uncertain climate change hazards in participatory climate change adaptation processes, Geoscience Communication 7, 121–144.
rights: CC BY 4.0; retain third-party credits shown in the article, including the source diagram and logos in Figure 3.
illustrates: A workshop slide connecting emissions scenarios, model chains, periods and hydrological indicators.
regional_adaptation: Replace the model chain with the local analysis provenance, exact windows and spatial support; keep it separate from findings.

title: Distinguish forced response from individual realizations
citation: Milinski, Maher and Olonscheck (2020), How large does a large ensemble need to be?, Earth System Dynamics 11, 885–901.
illustrates: Ensemble-size-dependent uncertainty around a large-ensemble forced-response estimate.
regional_adaptation: Explain whether a panel describes individual future realizations or estimated model forced responses. These are different quantities.

title: Make archive coverage visible
citation: Maher et al. (2025), The updated Multi-Model Large Ensemble Archive and the Climate Variability Diagnostics Package: new tools for the study of climate variability and change, Geoscientific Model Development 18, 6341–6365.
illustrates: Published archive inventory showing models, scenarios, variables and ensemble availability.
regional_adaptation: Translate this table into a model-by-scenario availability matrix with resolved counts, exclusions, missing variables and exact periods.

title: Show the models behind a mean-change summary
citation: Brunner et al. (2020), Reduced global warming from CMIP6 projections when weighting models by performance and independence, Earth System Dynamics 11, 995–1012.
illustrates: Individual model dots, weights and weighted/unweighted summaries across horizons and scenarios.
regional_adaptation: For a catchment, use temperature differences and precipitation absolute/relative changes, paired within each model before aggregation.

title: Catchment climate changes by month
citation: Perra, Piras, Deidda, Paniconi, Mascaro, Vivoni, Cau, Marras, Ludwig and Meyer (2018), Multimodel assessment of climate change-induced hydrologic impacts for a Mediterranean catchment, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 22, 4125–4143.
illustrates: Annual and monthly climate comparisons for a Mediterranean catchment, with individual climate models visible.
regional_adaptation: Borrow the monthly layout, but replace relative temperature changes with differences in degrees. Include absolute rainfall changes in dry months.

title: Compare the seasonal redistribution across catchments
citation: Hanus, Hrachowitz, Zekollari, Schoups, Vizcaino and Kaitna (2021), Future changes in annual, seasonal and monthly runoff signatures in contrasting Alpine catchments in Austria, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 3429–3453.
illustrates: Monthly change distributions separated by catchment and emissions scenario.
regional_adaptation: This figure shows runoff. Reuse its layout for monthly climate changes without interpreting runoff as a direct precipitation response.

title: Separate trajectories from the sources of their spread
citation: Lehner et al. (2020), Partitioning climate projection uncertainty with multiple large ensembles and CMIP5/6, Earth System Dynamics 11, 491–508.
illustrates: Smoothed temperature trajectories alongside absolute and fractional projection uncertainty.
regional_adaptation: For regional use, label smoothing and membership. A band of smoothed responses does not show annual weather variability.

title: Show changes across the year-to-year distribution
citation: Müller and Döll (2024), Quantifying and communicating uncertain climate change hazards in participatory climate change adaptation processes, Geoscience Communication 7, 121–144.
rights: CC BY 4.0; retain third-party credits shown in the article, including the source diagram and logos in Figure 3.
illustrates: Hydrological distribution changes summarized at several interannual quantiles.
regional_adaptation: For climate variables, retain separate member-level distributions and describe whether forced trends have been removed.

title: Check variability before constraining projections
citation: Suarez-Gutierrez and Maher (2026), Temperature variability projections remain uncertain after constraining them to best performing Large Ensembles of individual Climate Models, Nature Communications 17, 314.
illustrates: Temperature time series and rank histograms with and without detrending.
regional_adaptation: Use alongside regional variability changes to show whether models reproduce the relevant observed variability; avoid treating a passing rank diagnostic as complete validation.

title: Translate ensemble agreement into a readable summary
citation: Müller and Döll (2024), Quantifying and communicating uncertain climate change hazards in participatory climate change adaptation processes, Geoscience Communication 7, 121–144.
rights: CC BY 4.0; retain third-party credits shown in the article, including the source diagram and logos in Figure 3.
illustrates: An alternative workshop summary of annual and seasonal hydrological changes by horizon and scenario.
regional_adaptation: State sign agreement as a contributor count. For scenario contrasts, add common-membership paired differences; this slide does not provide that diagnostic.

title: Expose record-length and ensemble-size sensitivity
citation: Milinski, Maher and Olonscheck (2020), How large does a large ensemble need to be?, Earth System Dynamics 11, 885–901.
illustrates: Variability estimates examined against ensemble size and 30-year versus 100-year records.
regional_adaptation: Add a compact sensitivity panel for the suite's actual window choices. Sample-size sensitivity is distinct from model structural uncertainty.

title: Check sensitivity to ensemble dependence
citation: Brunner et al. (2020), Reduced global warming from CMIP6 projections when weighting models by performance and independence, Earth System Dynamics 11, 995–1012.
illustrates: A controlled dependence experiment showing how weights respond to a member treated as a separate model.
regional_adaptation: Compare equal-model, family-aware and leave-family-out summaries; report weight concentration and changed conclusions.

title: Preserve the joint temperature-precipitation signal
citation: Christensen, Kjellström, Dieterich, Gröger and Meier (2022), Atmospheric regional climate projections for the Baltic Sea region until 2100, Earth System Dynamics 13, 133–157.
illustrates: Paired regional temperature and precipitation changes, faceted by season and spatial support.
regional_adaptation: Keep model/member identity paired and add horizon facets. Do not construct a hot-dry projection by combining marginal quantiles.

title: Show why uncertainty depends on region and variable
citation: Lehner et al. (2020), Partitioning climate projection uncertainty with multiple large ensembles and CMIP5/6, Earth System Dynamics 11, 491–508.
illustrates: Global and regional examples combining trajectories with fractional uncertainty components.
regional_adaptation: Use regional panels and actual ensemble hierarchy. Component fractions depend on the partition method; show its assumptions and residual bias.

title: Display estimation error rather than only ensemble spread
citation: Milinski, Maher and Olonscheck (2020), How large does a large ensemble need to be?, Earth System Dynamics 11, 885–901.
illustrates: Error of an estimated forced response as a function of ensemble size.
regional_adaptation: This is a member-subsampling example, not a temporal block bootstrap. For finite climate records, preserve serial dependence and report block/window sensitivity separately.

title: Make weighting choices inspectable
citation: Brunner et al. (2020), Reduced global warming from CMIP6 projections when weighting models by performance and independence, Earth System Dynamics 11, 995–1012.
illustrates: Performance, independence and combined weights shown against an equal-weight reference.
regional_adaptation: Show all weights and their concentration. Diagnostics trained on global temperature need independent justification for local precipitation or extremes.

title: Test whether weighting improves held-out predictions
citation: Brunner et al. (2020), Reduced global warming from CMIP6 projections when weighting models by performance and independence, Earth System Dynamics 11, 995–1012.
illustrates: Perfect-model tests comparing weighting diagnostics and their skill relative to an unweighted ensemble.
regional_adaptation: Prefer held-out families and independent observations when possible; keep the unweighted regional result visible.

title: Connect warming levels to scenario-dependent dates
citation: Gu, Chen, Yin, Sullivan, Wang, Guo, Zhang and Kim (2020), Projected increases in magnitude and socioeconomic exposure of global droughts in 1.5 and 2 °C warmer climates, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 24, 451–472.
illustrates: Scenario warming trajectories with crossing dates for selected global temperature levels.
regional_adaptation: Implement crossings per model/member, not from a scenario-mean curve. Document the global baseline and crossing rule; record unreached levels explicitly.

title: Show that equal warming need not imply equal regional conditions
citation: Roldán-Gómez, De Luca, Bernardello and Donat (2025), Regional irreversibility of mean and extreme surface air temperature and precipitation in CMIP6 overshoot scenarios associated with interhemispheric temperature asymmetries, Earth System Dynamics 16, 1–27.
illustrates: Regional extreme-temperature trajectories plotted against both time and global temperature on an overshoot pathway.
regional_adaptation: Retain warming and cooling branches; do not average them together. Use this as a path-dependence diagnostic.

title: Compare robustness at grid and regional scales
citation: IPCC (2021), Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis, Working Group I contribution to the Sixth Assessment Report, Atlas, Figure Atlas.9, Cambridge University Press.
rights: IPCC copyright; unmodified limited reproduction for personal non-commercial use with full attribution. Do not redistribute or adapt this image under CC BY. See https://www.ipcc.ch/copyright/.
illustrates: IPCC assessment example of precipitation-extreme change and robustness across spatial scales.
regional_adaptation: Keep agreement, detectability and data coverage distinct. Use the documented robustness rules from the guide, with explicit contributor counts.

title: Make the emergence threshold visible
citation: de Vries, Sippel, Pendergrass and Knutti (2023), Robust global detection of forced changes in mean and extreme precipitation despite observational disagreement on the magnitude of change, Earth System Dynamics 14, 81–100.
illustrates: Signal-to-noise trajectories with a threshold and alternative observational/method choices.
regional_adaptation: This is global observational detection. For a catchment projection, define local signal, noise, persistence and non-emergence explicitly.

title: Compare extreme-precipitation outcomes at a warming level
citation: Bevacqua, Fischer, Sillmann and Zscheischler (2026), Moderate global warming does not rule out extreme global climate outcomes, Nature.
illustrates: Rx5day changes with multimodel summaries and coherent selected-model extreme outcomes.
regional_adaptation: Use daily inputs and fixed indicator definitions. A precipitation extreme is a hazard indicator, not an estimate of local flood damage.

title: Show how the change depends on event rarity
citation: Hanus, Hrachowitz, Zekollari, Schoups, Vizcaino and Kaitna (2021), Future changes in annual, seasonal and monthly runoff signatures in contrasting Alpine catchments in Austria, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 3429–3453.
illustrates: Catchment flood-magnitude changes against return period, with ensemble spread.
regional_adaptation: A hydrological analogue for climate-extreme curves. State the fitting model, sample length and interval meaning; avoid extrapolating rare tails without support.

title: Hold the reference event fixed when comparing frequency
citation: Gu, Chen, Yin, Sullivan, Wang, Guo, Zhang and Kim (2020), Projected increases in magnitude and socioeconomic exposure of global droughts in 1.5 and 2 °C warmer climates, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 24, 451–472.
illustrates: Maps of future joint return periods for a reference drought event.
regional_adaptation: Distinguish joint and marginal return periods, and define the exceedance event. An event's future frequency differs from its future return-level magnitude.

title: Show drought duration and severity separately
citation: Gu, Chen, Yin, Sullivan, Wang, Guo, Zhang and Kim (2020), Projected increases in magnitude and socioeconomic exposure of global droughts in 1.5 and 2 °C warmer climates, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 24, 451–472.
illustrates: Paired maps of drought duration and severity changes derived from SPEI.
regional_adaptation: Use a fixed reference fit and documented PET method; show precipitation-only and water-balance indicators together.

title: Show how drought definitions affect results
citation: Gu, Chen, Yin, Sullivan, Wang, Guo, Zhang and Kim (2020), Projected increases in magnitude and socioeconomic exposure of global droughts in 1.5 and 2 °C warmer climates, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 24, 451–472.
illustrates: Comparison of drought-characteristic distributions under alternative detection thresholds.
regional_adaptation: Label whether distributions are across locations, years or models. Spatial distributions of ensemble-mean results are not model uncertainty.

title: Explain a compound event through its physical sequence
citation: Shepherd et al. (2018), Storylines: an alternative approach to representing uncertainty in physical aspects of climate change, Climatic Change 151, 555–571.
rights: Article: CC BY 4.0. Figure 1 includes separately credited photographs: panel c, Bern cantonal police, used with permission; panel d, a credited external website. Do not assume those photographs can be redistributed under the article license. Saved whole and unchanged for personal research reference.
illustrates: An Alpine rain-on-snow event connecting synoptic conditions, temperature, rainfall and snow.
regional_adaptation: Use an event timeline plus process sketch for local storylines; estimate occurrence frequencies separately from the conditional narrative.

title: Keep spatially concurrent drought fields coherent
citation: Bevacqua, Fischer, Sillmann and Zscheischler (2026), Moderate global warming does not rule out extreme global climate outcomes, Nature.
illustrates: Drought-frequency outcomes across breadbasket regions using coherent model fields.
regional_adaptation: For multi-catchment exposure, retain the same model/member across all locations. Location-by-location worst cases may never occur together.

title: Distinguish timing, length and amount
citation: Dunning, Black and Allan (2018), Later wet seasons with more intense rainfall over Africa under future climate change, Journal of Climate 31, 9719–9738.
rights: © 2018 American Meteorological Society. Open access is stated, but the publisher page does not grant a CC license. Saved for personal research reference; redistribution/adaptation permission has not been verified. Publisher reuse-policy page was blocked.
illustrates: Wet-season onset, cessation, length and rainfall amount shown as separate mapped changes.
regional_adaptation: Use locally meaningful season definitions. A timing shift is not equivalent to a change in rainfall during fixed calendar months.

title: Link a regional timing shift to rainy-day characteristics
citation: Dunning, Black and Allan (2018), Later wet seasons with more intense rainfall over Africa under future climate change, Journal of Climate 31, 9719–9738.
rights: © 2018 American Meteorological Society. Open access is stated, but the publisher page does not grant a CC license. Saved for personal research reference; redistribution/adaptation permission has not been verified. Publisher reuse-policy page was blocked.
illustrates: Regional trajectories of onset, total rain, wet-day intensity and wet-day count.
regional_adaptation: Use daily data for onset and wet-day metrics; label smoothing and replace the single spread band with clearly separated scenario distributions if needed.

title: Evaluate the timescales of a climate mode
citation: Maher et al. (2025), The updated Multi-Model Large Ensemble Archive and the Climate Variability Diagnostics Package: new tools for the study of climate variability and change, Geoscientific Model Development 18, 6341–6365.
illustrates: ENSO power spectra comparing model ensembles and observations.
regional_adaptation: Pair spectral diagnostics with regional teleconnections; global mode skill alone does not establish local seasonal rainfall skill.

title: Compare teleconnection patterns with observational uncertainty
citation: Maher et al. (2025), The updated Multi-Model Large Ensemble Archive and the Climate Variability Diagnostics Package: new tools for the study of climate variability and change, Geoscientific Model Development 18, 6341–6365.
illustrates: La Niña precipitation composites, model-observation differences and observed ranks in model ensembles.
regional_adaptation: For a local summary, add season-specific regional effects with event counts. Distinguish changed mode amplitude from changed teleconnection strength.

title: Connect changing snow storage to seasonal water supply
citation: Hanus, Hrachowitz, Zekollari, Schoups, Vizcaino and Kaitna (2021), Future changes in annual, seasonal and monthly runoff signatures in contrasting Alpine catchments in Austria, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 3429–3453.
illustrates: Monthly melt contributions for historical and future catchment conditions.
regional_adaptation: Retain elevation and snow regime context. Snowmelt projections require snow/process information beyond monthly temperature and precipitation alone.

title: Expose differences in evaporative-demand estimates
citation: Perra, Piras, Deidda, Paniconi, Mascaro, Vivoni, Cau, Marras, Ludwig and Meyer (2018), Multimodel assessment of climate change-induced hydrologic impacts for a Mediterranean catchment, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 22, 4125–4143.
illustrates: Annual, monthly and model-specific potential evapotranspiration comparisons.
regional_adaptation: Document the PET formulation and required meteorological variables. PET is atmospheric demand and cannot be equated with actual evapotranspiration.

title: Give each regional result a spatial-support context
citation: Hanus, Hrachowitz, Zekollari, Schoups, Vizcaino and Kaitna (2021), Future changes in annual, seasonal and monthly runoff signatures in contrasting Alpine catchments in Austria, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 3429–3453.
illustrates: Catchment boundaries, elevation, observation stations and precipitation zones.
regional_adaptation: Add source-grid footprints and effective cell counts for projections; distinguish catchments, subcatchments and station observations.

title: Compare national distributions with clear denominators
citation: Gu, Chen, Yin, Sullivan, Wang, Guo, Zhang and Kim (2020), Projected increases in magnitude and socioeconomic exposure of global droughts in 1.5 and 2 °C warmer climates, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 24, 451–472.
illustrates: Country panels showing spatial distributions of changes in a reference drought event's return period.
regional_adaptation: These distributions are across grid cells, not climate models. State the spatial denominator and keep physical hazard separate from population/GDP exposure.

title: Explain what bias adjustment preserves
citation: Lange (2019), Trend-preserving bias adjustment and statistical downscaling with ISIMIP3BASD (v1.0), Geoscientific Model Development 12, 3055–3070.
illustrates: CDF schematics illustrating alternative transfers of a simulated change signal to observations.
regional_adaptation: State whether changes are additive, multiplicative or mixed. Evaluate tails, wet-day frequency and dependence separately.

title: Check the spatial structures introduced by downscaling
citation: Lange (2019), Trend-preserving bias adjustment and statistical downscaling with ISIMIP3BASD (v1.0), Geoscientific Model Development 12, 3055–3070.
illustrates: Comparison of precipitation fields produced by different downscaling steps.
regional_adaptation: Use matched GCM/member/time inputs. Inspect catchment totals and cross-catchment dependence; finer grids alone do not demonstrate added skill.

title: Show the tradeoff between adjustment and change preservation
citation: Lange (2019), Trend-preserving bias adjustment and statistical downscaling with ISIMIP3BASD (v1.0), Geoscientific Model Development 12, 3055–3070.
illustrates: A performance comparison separating correction of historical distributions from preservation of trends.
regional_adaptation: Repeat relevant diagnostics by region, season and variable with held-out data; a method that adjusts means can still damage extremes or dependence.

title: Start with system performance across stressors
citation: Lachaut and Tilmant (2021), Possibilistic response surfaces: incorporating fuzzy thresholds into bottom-up flood vulnerability analysis, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 6421–6435.
illustrates: A bottom-up flood-control response surface, with reliability shown across two inflow stressors.
regional_adaptation: Add the decision threshold. These axes are inflow volume and dispersion, not temperature and precipitation: use a response surface in the independently selected CST stressors and retain its reference definitions.

title: Place projection evidence over a vulnerability domain
citation: Lachaut and Tilmant (2021), Possibilistic response surfaces: incorporating fuzzy thresholds into bottom-up flood vulnerability analysis, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 6421–6435.
illustrates: GCM-derived projection points over alternative fitted representations of an acceptability domain in inflow space.
regional_adaptation: Map projections into exactly the same stressors and reference definitions as the response surface; do not plot WF2 temperature/precipitation changes directly on these inflow axes. Point density is not calibrated climate probability.

title: Check colour accessibility before sharing
citation: Crameri, Shephard and Heron (2020), The misuse of colour in science communication, Nature Communications 11, 5444.
illustrates: Colour-map comparisons under several forms of colour-vision deficiency and in greyscale.
regional_adaptation: Choose a perceptually uniform palette appropriate to the variable; add labels and symbols so colour is not the only encoding.

title: Assess comprehension as well as visual preference
citation: Bannister et al. (2021), Improving the visual communication of environmental model projections, Scientific Reports 11, 19157.
illustrates: Display rankings across accuracy, confidence/ease and preference.
regional_adaptation: For the suite's regional summary, test retrieval of change magnitude, ensemble disagreement and threshold implications with intended readers.

title: Check both distributions and event timing
citation: Hanus, Hrachowitz, Zekollari, Schoups, Vizcaino and Kaitna (2021), Future changes in annual, seasonal and monthly runoff signatures in contrasting Alpine catchments in Austria, Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 25, 3429–3453.
illustrates: Catchment ECDFs and monthly distributions comparing observed and simulated historical climate and runoff.
regional_adaptation: Extend the ECDF layout to reference/future climate distributions. Keep magnitude, timing and model evaluation separate, and label each distribution's sampling unit.

title: Retain paired warming and precipitation return-level changes
citation: Christensen, Kjellström, Dieterich, Gröger and Meier (2022), Atmospheric regional climate projections for the Baltic Sea region until 2100, Earth System Dynamics 13, 133–157.
illustrates: Regional changes in a daily-precipitation 10-year return level plotted against temperature change.
regional_adaptation: Label the fitted distribution and reference event. Preserve each model's paired values and report finite-record sampling intervals separately from model spread.
